The VVitch, was the official feature film debut for Anya Taylor-Joy in a credited role. Prior to this film, Anya Taylor-Joy had filmed a minor role as a "Feeder Girl" in Vampire Academy (2014), but her scene was ultimately cut from the final theatrical release, making The Witch her first official on-screen credit.

Stephen King, who is often called the "master of horror", has stated that he was terrified by this film. King noted that the film is "tense and thought-provoking as well as visceral". He remarked that it stands out because it achieves deep, unsettling psychological dread unlike most modern horror releases. Directed by Robert Eggers, The Witch follows a Puritan family experiencing supernatural forces in the New England woods in the 1630s.

source_details.title: Vampire Academy
source_details.synopsis: Vampire Academy is a 2014 American fantasy comedy film directed by Mark Waters from a screenplay by his brother Daniel Waters, based on the first book of the novel series of the same name by Richelle Mead. The film stars an ensemble cast led by Zoey Deutch as Rose Hathaway, a Dhampir, and Lucy Fry as Lissa Dragomir, her Moroi best friend, and follows their return to the St Vladimir's Academy boarding school, after being on the run for one year. Preger Entertainment announced the film's development in 2010, with Don Murphy as producer. In 2012, the Waters brothers joined the project with Mark serving as director and Daniel as screenwriter.
